stem: The point \((3, -4)\) lies on the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane. The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(-x) + 3\). Which of the following points must lie on the graph of \(y = g(x)\)?
solution: To use \(f(3) = -4\), the input of \(f\) must be 3, so \(-x = 3\) and \(x = -3\).
Graphically: \(f(-x)\) reflects the graph across the \(y\)-axis, sending \((3, -4)\) to \((-3, -4)\); adding 3 then shifts it up to \((-3, -1)\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This ignores the \(-x\). \(g(3) = f(-3) + 3\), and \(f(-3)\) is not known.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reflects the point across the \(x\)-axis (changing \(-4\) to \(4\)) and then adds 3. The \(-x\) reflects across the \(y\)-axis, so it is the \(x\)-coordinate that changes sign.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The definition of \(g\) adds 3 to the output of \(f\): \(-4 + 3 = -1\), not \(-4 - 3 = -7\).

verify:
assert choices[answer] == r'\((-3, -1)\)'
f = Function('f')
x = symbols('x')
g = f(-x) + 3
assert g.subs(x, -3).subs(f(3), -4) == -1
assert len(set(choices.values())) == 4
